lines.trans: My sales record this month was number one!
Really? Unbelievable!
Next time, I'll buy you a Licca-chan House.
That's an absolute promise, okay!
And for Daisuke, I'll buy a Countach RC car.
Are you sure about that, making a promise like that?
Yeah, it's fine.
Let's move to a bigger house, okay?
I'm looking forward to it.

words.gloss: something to look forward to; fun

lines.trans: Yeah, yeah, leave it to me.
Still, isn't it great that work is going well?
I'm counting on you.

Still, isn't it great that work is going well?
I'm counting on you.
Good night, see you tomorrow.

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in state

meanings.note: After a te-form (積んでおきました, contracted 入っとけ), indicates doing something in advance or staying put.

examples.text: 窓を開けておきました。
ここに置いておきます。
examples.trans: I will leave it here for now.

meanings.note: Casual or warm farewell said before going to sleep (polite: おやすみなさい).

examples.text: もう遅いからおやすみ。
examples.trans: It's late already, so good night.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Repeated はい, used to reassure someone or casually acknowledge what they said.

examples.text: はいはい、分かりました。

examples.trans: Yeah, yeah, leave it to me.

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Iconic Italian supercar popular in 1970s–80s Japan, including as toys and models.

examples.text: カウンタックはかっこいい。
カウンタックのラジコン。

meanings.note: Abbreviation of ラジオコントロール (radio control).

examples.text: 誕生日にラジコンを買ってもらいました。
examples.trans: I got an RC car for my birthday.

examples.text: 公園でラジコンを走らせます。
examples.trans: I run my RC car in the park.

meanings.note: Combines 一 (one) with 位 (rank/place).

examples.text: クラスで一位になりました。
examples.trans: I got first place in my class.

examples.text: 今月の成績は一位でした。
examples.trans: This month's results were number one.

meanings.note: Refers to the upcoming occasion or a recent/current occasion.

examples.text: 今度一緒に食事しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's have a meal together next time.

examples.text: 今度の休みはどこへ行きますか。
examples.trans: Where are you going on your next day off?

meanings.note: Temporal noun combining 今 (now) and 月 (month).

examples.text: 今月はとても忙しいです。
examples.trans: I am very busy this month.

examples.text: 今月の目標を達成しました。

meanings.note: Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; potential form 信じられる means 'can believe' (信じられない = unbelievable).

examples.text: あなたの言葉を信じます。
そんなこと、信じられません。
examples.trans: I can't believe such a thing.

meanings.note: Compound noun combining 営業 (sales/business) and 成績 (results/record).

examples.text: 今月の営業成績は一位でした。
examples.trans: This month's sales record was number one.

examples.text: 営業成績を上げるために努力しています。
examples.trans: I am working hard to improve my sales performance.

meanings.note: Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Noun (いえ).

examples.text: 駅の近くに新しい家を建てた。
examples.trans: I built a new house near the station.

examples.text: 今日はずっと家にいます。
examples.trans: I'll be at home all day today.

meanings.note: I-adjective describing large area or space.

examples.text: この部屋はとても広いです。
広い庭のある家に住みたいです。
examples.trans: I want to live in a house with a big yard.

meanings.note: Godan verb; volitional form 引っ越そう means 'let's move'.

examples.text: 来月東京に引っ越します。
examples.trans: I am moving to Tokyo next month.

examples.text: もっと広い家に引っ越そうな。
examples.trans: Let's move to a bigger house, okay?

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
Noun; takes する.

examples.text: みんなから期待されている。
examples.trans: Everyone has high expectations for me.

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.
